_comment: written once and checked against four implementations: the Rust resolver,
the JavaScript the Cloudflare adapter generates, `iyo serve`, and a live
origin via `iyo conform`. They are measured against this file rather than
against each other, so agreeing on a wrong answer still fails.
Cases name a subject role, not a path, so the same sentences run on the
fixture and on a deployment. Roles are resolved by one resolver in Rust:

cases.name: a browser gets the page
cases.subject: term

cases.name: turtle is redirected to its sibling
cases.subject: term

cases.name: json-ld is redirected to its sibling
cases.subject: term

cases.name: markdown is redirected to its sibling
cases.subject: term

cases.name: a bare wildcard gets the default
cases.subject: term

cases.name: q-values rank html above turtle
cases.subject: term

cases.name: q-values rank turtle above html
cases.subject: term

cases.name: an explicit type beats a wildcard whatever the q-values say
cases.subject: term

cases.name: a client that asked only for rdf gets rdf
cases.subject: term

cases.name: no accept header gets the default
cases.subject: term

cases.name: a type nobody publishes gets the default rather than a 406
cases.subject: term

cases.name: q=0 means not that one
cases.subject: term

cases.name: format overrides accept
cases.subject: term

cases.name: connegp mediatype overrides accept
cases.subject: term

cases.name: a term the site owns the name of is served from its directory
cases.subject: dir-term

cases.name: a term served from a directory keeps its layout
cases.subject: dir-term

cases.name: a request naming a representation is not a negotiation
cases.subject: sibling

cases.name: a name that is not a term does not resolve
cases.subject: absent-name

cases.name: a namespace document is not a term
cases.subject: namespace

cases.name: a nested namespace is not a term of its parent
cases.subject: nested-namespace

cases.name: a term inside a release negotiates like the newest one
cases.subject: release-term

cases.name: and redirects to the sibling inside that release
cases.subject: release-term

cases.name: a name that is not a term is not one inside a release either
cases.subject: absent-release-name

cases.name: a segment that is not a release is left to the file layer
cases.subject: absent-release

cases.name: a case variant of a term does not resolve to it
cases.subject: case-variant

cases.name: a reserved segment does not resolve as a term's turtle sibling
cases.subject: reserved-segment

cases.name: a path below a term is not a term
cases.subject: sub-term-path

cases.name: an extension nobody publishes is not a negotiation
cases.subject: sibling-unpublished

cases.name: a namespace with no terms matches no name
cases.subject: empty-namespace
